title: Deduction, Collection and Recovery of Tax
outcomes: Describe the TDS framework under sections 392 to 398.
Apply key TDS rates and thresholds for residents.
Compute consequences of default and higher rates.
Apply advance tax and recovery provisions.

meta.exam_tip: For each payment state payer status, table entry, threshold and rate in one line.

concepts.title: Framework of tax deduction at source
body: Chapter XIX of the Income-tax Act, 2025 collects tax as income arises. Section 392 covers TDS on salary at average rates; section 393 consolidates other TDS in tables — Table 1 for residents (393(1)), Table 2 for non-residents (393(2)) and Table 3 for others (393(3)) — with exemptions in 393(4). Section 394 covers TCS.

Tax is generally deducted on the earlier of crediting the payee and paying him (subject to specific rules), and deposited within prescribed time. Deductors obtain TAN (section 397), file quarterly statements and issue certificates; payees claim credit through Form 26AS/AIS.

A "specified person" (non-individuals, and individuals/HUFs with prior-year business turnover above ₹1 crore or professional receipts above ₹50 lakh) is liable to deduct under several entries; other individuals deduct only under specific ones (e.g. high rent, property purchase).
concepts.analogy: Deduct when you pay or credit, deposit on time, report quarterly.
concepts.work: A salaried individual buying a flat for ₹60 lakh must deduct 1% though not otherwise a deductor.

concepts.title: Key TDS provisions for residents
body: Common entries: insurance commission (2% individuals, 10% companies); rent — 2% where payer is not a specified person and rent exceeds ₹50,000 a month, and for specified persons 2% on plant and machinery or 10% on land and buildings; 1% on purchase of immovable property of ₹50 lakh or more (using the higher of consideration and stamp value).

Contractors: 1% (individual/HUF) or 2% (others) above ₹30,000 per payment or ₹1,00,000 aggregate; professional fees, royalty and non-compete fees 10% and fees for technical services or call centres 2% above ₹50,000; directors' remuneration 10% with no threshold; dividends 10% above ₹10,000 to individuals by non-cash modes; bank interest 10% above ₹50,000 (₹1,00,000 for senior citizens); interest by others 10% above ₹10,000.

Purchase of goods: buyers with prior-year turnover above ₹10 crore deduct 0.1% on purchases from a seller exceeding ₹50 lakh. VDA transfers: 1%. Lottery winnings 30%. Life insurance payouts: 2% on the income component.
concepts.analogy: Know the payer, the rate and the threshold.
concepts.work: Office rent of ₹70,000 a month paid by a company bears 10% TDS.

concepts.title: Tax collection at source
body: Section 394 makes sellers collect tax: on scrap, tendu leaves, forest produce and minerals at specified rates; and 1% on sale of a motor vehicle or notified luxury goods (watches, art, yachts, designer bags and others) worth more than ₹10 lakh each.

Authorised dealers collect TCS on LRS remittances above ₹10 lakh in aggregate: 2% for education or medical treatment and 20% for other purposes; none where remittance is out of an education loan from a financial institution. Sellers of overseas tour packages collect 2%.
TCS is collected at the time of debit or receipt, whichever is earlier, and is credited to the buyer's tax account.
concepts.analogy: Sellers and dealers collect tax at source on specified receipts.
concepts.work: A car sold for ₹12 lakh attracts TCS of ₹12,000.

concepts.title: Consequences of default and higher rates
body: A payer who fails to deduct or pay is an assessee in default (section 398) — unless the payee has filed a return, included the income and paid tax, certified by an accountant. Interest is 1% a month from when tax was deductible to deduction, and 1.5% a month from deduction to payment.

Non-furnishing of PAN (section 397) means deduction at the higher of the specified rate and 20% (with specific caps for some items), and TCS at the higher of twice the rate and 5% (max 20%). For specified non-filers, higher TDS/TCS rates may apply.
Expenditure where TDS is not deducted suffers disallowance — 30% for resident payments and full disallowance for non-resident payments — until the tax is paid.
concepts.analogy: Defaults cost interest, disallowance and possibly penalty.
concepts.work: A two-month delay in deducting ₹20,000 costs ₹400 of interest.

concepts.title: Advance tax and self-assessment
body: Advance tax is payable where estimated tax after TDS/TCS is ₹10,000 or more: 15%, 45%, 75% and 100% by 15 June, 15 September, 15 December and 15 March. Presumptive taxpayers under section 58 may pay the whole by 15 March. Resident senior citizens with no business income are exempt.
Interest is charged for default in payment of advance tax and for deferment of instalments; self-assessment tax with interest is payable before filing the return.
Recovery provisions allow the AO and TRO to attach bank accounts and property, recover from debtors and from directors of private companies in specified cases.
concepts.analogy: Pay as you earn, quarter by quarter.
concepts.work: A consultant with estimated tax of ₹2 lakh pays ₹30,000 by 15 June.

illustrations.title: TDS for a company payer
illustrations.q: Sarovar Ltd (turnover ₹60 crore last year) pays in T.Y. 2026-27: (a) to Mohan, an individual contractor, ₹25,000, ₹28,000 and ₹60,000 under one contract; (b) professional fees of ₹45,000 to Dr. Rao (only payment); (c) office rent of ₹70,000 a month to Lata, an individual; (d) ₹80,00,000 to one supplier for goods. All payees furnished PAN. Compute TDS.

illustrations.q: Tax of ₹20,000 was deductible on 10 June 2026 but was deducted on 10 August 2026 and paid to the government on 20 September 2026. Compute interest under section 398 (count each month or part).

jobs.title: Monthly TDS review
jobs.situation: The company's vendor payments for the month need TDS checks.
steps: Classify each payment by table entry.
jobs.takeaway: Classification errors are the commonest TDS defaults.

mcqs.explain: Per vehicle. In practice: credited to buyer.

mcqs.explain: Non-education, non-medical. In practice: credit in return.

viva.q: Who is a specified person for TDS?
viva.model: Any person other than an individual or HUF, and individuals or HUFs whose prior-year business turnover exceeded ₹1 crore or professional receipts ₹50 lakh.

viva.q: When is a payer not an assessee in default despite not deducting?
viva.model: When the payee has filed a return including the income and paid the tax, supported by an accountant's certificate.

viva.q: What is the TCS on an overseas tour package?
What disallowance follows non-deduction on a resident payment?
viva.model: Thirty percent of the expense, allowed in the year the tax is paid.

viva.q: Who need not pay advance tax?
viva.model: Resident senior citizens whose income is only from heads other than business or profession.
